[b]Neue Republik Lawsuit Against the Government of Thyven Regarding the White Strait[/b]

[i]The delegation of the Neue Republik (New Republic) to the International Alliance requests that litigation begin regarding the government of Thyvens actions in the White Strait. 

As of October 13th, 2026, the Thyven government has begun imposing a 20% toll on the total value of Republik goods shipped through its territorial waters in the White Strait. As a part of a larger group of punitive measures including 200% tariffs and sanctions, the tolls imposed represent an attack by the government of Thyven on Republik commercial shipping and free trade as a whole. 

Specifically, as regarding international law, the Republik believes that the actions of the government of Thyven are in stark violation of the International Alliance Convention on the Laws of the Sea or IACLOS. Article twenty-six, section two, of the IACLOS states that: No charge may be levied upon foreign ships by reason only of their passage through the territorial sea. (IACLOS p.27)

These rights, afforded by the international maritime rights to innocent passage undergird the free trade and shipping that support the global economy. The commercial ships of the Republik passing through the White Strait have not committed any violations, as defined by IACLOS that would disqualify them from innocent passage. The government of Thyven has presented no credible evidence to domestic or international authorities that the ships of the Republik have engaged in pollution, espionage, undue military use or any other violation of maritime law. 

The Republik requests that the International Alliance work to end the illegal actions of the government of Thyven, seek compensation for the Republiks economic losses as a result of international crime and reaffirm maritime law. [/i]

[quote=dhornaper;60520472]Across the Shamatine border in Dhornaper, President Ayub Khan, 75 years old and in slow decline from the energetic and aggressive person he once was, reads the ULR newspapers and Foreign Ministry dispatches brought before him.

He sits near a lit fire and reads it slowly through his glasses while his foreign minister stands. "The assassin has damned his country," he says to his Foreign Minister. "To attempt to assassinate the king would have provoked an uproar against him had he succeeded. I would have tortured him to death if I was the king. But he failed, and there were vultures ready to take adadvantage of any political chaos."

"Sire," the foreign Minister says, erroneously using the title he once used with deposed king Jalaludin Shah, Ayub Khan's cousin, "the king survived and has returned to ULR's southern central island, the military has revolted around the eastern command, and violent revolutionaries have sprung up in the west. I am concerned about the spillover into our country."

Ayub Khan doesn't correct the royal title he is addressed by; he is used to being treated as a king by the population given that Presidents and Republics are still a novel concept in Dhornaper. "I am not worried and I am sure there is some opportunity for us to get involved to our benefit too. You must talk with the defence minister and treasury minister. They must know about it and must see how we can benefit from it."

"I am tired, and have much to do. You are dismissed." The foreign minister takes his leave while Ayub Khan returns to slowly reading through newspapers and dispatches from his ministers, keeping the events of ULR away from his mind until more comes of it.[/quote]
(The king retreated to a royal compound, in the southern center of Sabrata. He only intends to flee to Lavia if his forces are entirely overcome)

[quote=the_crystalline_empire;60516341]Villiard seemed ready to respond to the philosophical angle of the sanguinans, but was stopped by a simple motion from the cardinal, for they had come near to where they were supposed to arrive.

Indeed we shall discuss these terms, but with more proficiently minded people who know the details of trade and negotiation, now look, we arrive! He said.

The cars had sufficiently left the environs of the port city, and now were driving down a suburban gravel driveway towards a large neatly maintained Chateau.

Missir and madame, I fear I shouldve informed you, but, the king of Montfleur has arranged to meet you and for you to meet the other necessary figures, at a party hosted by the Duchess De Lorraine, the incumbent head of our government and a gracious host, stated the Cardinal as the cars came to a stop before the entry doors, revealing a curious entourage that had gathered along the side of the driveway.[/quote]
"... [i]Possiamo fare festa?[/i]..." Terrasi asked, poking her head out of the car.

"[i]Probabilmente[/i]." Lo Pilato swiftly responded, encouraging her, almost pushing her to step out. "[i]Assicurati solo che il nostro governo abbia una bella immagine[/i]. We've been working a lot these past few days. Happiness always seems so far away in the doing of good."

The Sanguinians walked into the entourage together and immersed itself in the crowd, greeting guests with their names as they were guided into the party.
